approval.cohort: Fourteen completed presidencies, Truman through Biden, ending January 2025
approval.limits: Tenures differ in length. Survey counts and weights are unspecified. This cohort is not inauguration approval or single-poll variability, and partisan polarization makes stationarity uncertain.

midterm.cohort: Nineteen midterms from 1950 through 2022, signed for the sitting President's party
midterm.unit: percentage points of national two-party House vote share
midterm.limits: Source rounds changes to one decimal and excludes unopposed districts where no vote was recorded. Approval averages and midterm changes are unpaired observations; these data establish no causal response coefficient.

derived.limits: Arithmetic over rounded observations; this sample SD describes observed outcomes, not residual model error. Observed extremes are not proven future bounds.

coverage: United States national observations spanning elections across states; not separate state, territorial or local response estimates.
integrationLimits: These cohorts are not paired with each other and establish no approval-to-vote or economy-to-approval response coefficient.
No production world draw, current approval poll, population drift, election result or causal effect is defined by this packet.
No normal distribution, future hard bound, residual error distribution or uniform response-strength range is established.
World creation must save any approved calibration once; reading and reopening a save must not sample. No approved sampling specification is implemented here.

responseModels.name: Tufte 1975
responseModels.inputs: N8 is presidential-party average House vote percentage over eight prior elections; P is September Gallup approval percentage; deltaE is election-year real disposable personal income per capita change in 1958 dollars.
gaps: The candidate does not supply the complete N8 and real-income inputs. GDP growth is not this income variable.
An independent historical swing mean cannot replace N8 or be added to this intercept.
No residual SD was verified; mean absolute error and coefficient standard errors do not establish it.

responseModels.name: Cory McCartan midterms-22
responseModels.inputs: October/latest pre-November poll approval logit; quarterly GDP and CPI year-over-year changes; logged unemployment; retirements; polarization; presidency and House control.
gaps: The inspected tree lacks the fitted intercept, seven regression coefficients, residual sigma and joint posterior.
The PCA loadings are not election-response coefficients. Saved prediction draws are not residual samples.
Raw source lineage, retirement denominator and an apparent repeated logistic transform in uncontested-vote imputation remain unresolved.

# National approval and midterm calibration source packet

Read-only research, accessed 2026-09-29. No code/claims edits or helpers. Four primary/collector sources used below. This is an internal handoff; parent owns integration and owner-report review.

## Approval observations

[Gallup historical statistics table](https://news.gallup.com/poll/116677/presidential-approval-ratings-gallup-historicalstatistics-trends.aspx), current table through January 2025; page publication/update date unspecified. Values below are percentage approval averages, not approval-minus-disapproval.

| President | Completed tenure | Overall average | First-term average | Second-term average |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Truman | Apr1945–Jan1953 |45.4|55.6|36.5|
| Eisenhower | Jan1953–Jan1961 |65.0|69.6|60.5|
| Kennedy | Jan1961–Nov1963 |70.1|70.1|—|
| Johnson | Nov1963–Jan1969 |55.1|74.2|50.3|
| Nixon | Jan1969–Aug1974 |49.0|55.8|34.4|
| Ford | Aug1974–Jan1977 |47.2|47.2|—|
| Carter | Jan1977–Jan1981 |45.5|45.5|—|
| Reagan | Jan1981–Jan1989 |52.8|50.3|55.3|
| G.H.W. Bush | Jan1989–Jan1993 |60.9|60.9|—|
| Clinton | Jan1993–Jan2001 |55.1|49.6|60.6|
| G.W. Bush | Jan2001–Jan2009 |49.4|62.2|36.5|
| Obama | Jan2009–Jan2017 |47.9|49.1|46.7|
| Trump I | Jan2017–Jan2021 |41.1|41.1|—|
| Biden | Jan2021–Jan2025 |42.2|42.2|—|

Denominator: 14 completed presidencies, or 22 observed first/second-term rows. These include abbreviated accession/resignation/death periods; “term” is not uniformly four years. Individual poll counts and averaging weights are unspecified. Equal sampling would give each row equal probability despite differing tenure lengths. It does not reproduce single-poll variability, inauguration approval, current conditions, or causation.

[Gallup January 17, 2025 article](https://news.gallup.com/poll/655298/biden-job-approval-second-lowest-among-post-wwii-presidents.aspx) confirms Biden's 42.2% completed-presidency average and the 14-president cohort (six at least 50%, eight below). It describes increased partisan polarization, cautioning against treating the historical cohort as stationary.

Researcher arithmetic on the 14 overall averages: equal-row mean **51.907142857%**, population SD **8.245471856 percentage points**, sample SD **8.556730530**, observed range **41.1–70.1%**. These are derived statistics, not Gallup-published distribution parameters. Prefer an explicitly identified empirical row sample if calibrating from observed values; the table does not establish a Gaussian distribution or a future bound. No recommended effect coefficient.

## Midterm House two-party vote-share change

[Brookings Vital Statistics index](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/vital-statistics-on-congress/) identifies April 2026 dataset update. [Table 2-2 PDF](https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2-2-Full.pdf), “Popular Vote and House Seats Won by Party, 1946–2024,” reports change since the preceding election in major-party vote share. Sign below is reoriented to the sitting President's party (R/D in the source denotes the gaining party).

| Midterm | President party | Change, percentage points |
|---|---|---:|
|1950|D|-3.2|
|1954|R|-2.6|
|1958|R|-5.0|
|1962|D|-2.3|
|1966|D|-6.0|
|1970|R|-3.4|
|1974|R|-5.8|
|1978|D|-2.8|
|1982|R|-5.2|
|1986|R|-2.4|
|1990|R|-0.1|
|1994|D|-6.3|
|1998|D|-0.3|
|2002|R|+2.3|
|2006|R|-5.4|
|2010|D|-9.0|
|2014|D|-3.4|
|2018|R|-4.9|
|2022|D|-2.9|

Computed from these 19 rounded source observations: mean **−3.615789474**, sample SD (denominator 18) **2.581399956**, population SD (denominator 19) **2.512550216**, minimum **−9.0**, maximum **+2.3**. Thus **−3.6 / 2.6 / −9 to +2.3 is verified if “spread” means sample SD**, not population SD. Unit is percentage points of national two-party House vote share; not seats, vote margin, or percent relative change. 1998's small vote-share loss coexists with seat gains.

Source excludes districts where candidates ran unopposed and no vote was recorded. It compiles historical references/FEC with latest update from MIT Election Data + Science Lab, not an independent Clerk-only replication. No Clerk source was added within the four-source budget. Source rounds changes to one decimal; derived precision is arithmetic precision, not greater measurement precision.

## What these samples support

They provide transparent historical national calibration cohorts for a seeded world-creation choice under the owner's rule. They do not establish deterministic outcomes, runtime resampling, causal approval/economy coefficients, local/state rates, or hard fictional limits. Tenure-average approval and midterm vote-share changes are different measures and are not paired causal observations in this packet. Any weighting, smoothing, modern-era restriction, or transformation is a separately named design choice; no such choice is silently inferred here.

# Published national midterm response model — bounded research handoff

Accessed September 29, 2026. Internal source packet; no game/source/claims edits or helpers. Parent owns integration.

## Directly specified model

Edward R. Tufte, *Determinants of the Outcomes of Midterm Congressional Elections*, American Political Science Review 69 (1975), pp.812–826, DOI [10.2307/1958391](https://doi.org/10.2307/1958391). [Author-hosted primary paper PDF](https://www.edwardtufte.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Determinants-of-the-outcomes-of-midterm-congressional-elections-1975.pdf), Tables 1–4, printed pp.816–820.

Published equation:

`V = N8 − 11.083 + 0.133 P + 0.035 ΔE + u`

- V: presidential party's nationwide two-party House vote percentage.
- N8: that party's average vote percentage in preceding eight congressional elections.
- P: September Gallup presidential approval percentage.
- ΔE: election-year change in real disposable personal income per capita, **1958 dollars**, not percentage growth.
- Estimation: eight midterms, 1938/1946/1950/1954/1958/1962/1966/1970; 1942 omitted.
- Coefficient standard errors: approval .033; income .006. R² .912; adjusted R² .88.
- Table 3 fitted absolute errors: 0/.8/.1/.6/1.8/.8/.4/.3 points; published mean absolute error .6 points.
- Table 4 five historical prediction errors: 2.1/1.6/.6/.3/1.9 points; published mean absolute error 1.3 points.
- Author cautions that extreme approval/economic values can cause overresponse; tiny historical sample limits applicability.

**No residual SD was verified in the paper.** MAE is not SD; parameter standard errors are not residual spread. Do not use either as a Gaussian shock sigma.

## Exact support / implementation boundary

This is a national observed association model with approval **0.133 vote-share points per approval point** and real-income **0.035 vote-share points per 1958 dollar per person**. These units cannot justify the candidate's .45 approval or .6 real-growth coefficients. It does not estimate .35 unemployment, .2 inflation, or an economy-to-approval response of 2.

The response is deviation from an eight-election baseline, not change from the immediately preceding presidential-year House election. Conversion requires that prior election's vote share: subtract V_previous from the entire equation. Replacing N8 with 50, or combining this intercept with the independent −3.6 historical swing mean, creates a different model and risks counting historical midterm loss twice.

September measured approval is different from a sampled full-tenure Gallup average. National aggregate regression does not identify individual causal behavior, modern stability, local electoral response, or a government-policy-to-economy producer. The paper's dollar variable also requires its exact real-income concept and price base; substituting GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, or arbitrary prosperity breaks the published specification.

## Additional primary research inspected; no interchangeable coefficients accepted

[Jacobson/Kernell author-hosted chapter, “Midterm Congressional Elections Revisited: A Test of the Theory”](https://pages.ucsd.edu/~skernell/documents/strategy6.pdf), Table 6.2, printed p.68. Its nine-case revised Tufte specification reports intercept −9.75, fall popularity .125, fall percentage income change .521, adjusted R² .65; a spring specification reports intercept −7.30, spring popularity .065, spring income change .691, adjusted R² .72. This shows estimates depend on timing/specification. Chapter publication vintage, exact income timing, and residual spread were not fully established in this bounded pass; these are **not integration-ready substitutes**.

[2024 published national research, “Forecasting Partisan Collective Accountability during the 2024 US Presidential and Congressional Elections”](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1049096524000854), Cambridge abstract search-readable, full text retrieval failed. Authors report that approval does not predict their congressional outcomes while incumbent-party brand does. No coefficients or residual distribution extracted; it supplies a reason to avoid presenting the older response as universal, not an alternative implementation model.

## Remaining gap

A transparent model **with all requested modern predictors and published residual spread** was not established. The older Tufte model supplies genuine measured approval/income response, but the candidate's five coefficients remain unsupported. A modern paired national series/refit or another fully inspected published specification is still required if the parent wants GDP-growth/unemployment/inflation channels or an approval-economy producer. No coefficient was invented and no tenure-average approval row was paired with a midterm outcome.

# McCartan midterms-22 source verification

**Not integration-ready as a portable response model.** Read-only GitHub connector inspection at pinned tree/commit `c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271`, September 29, 2026; no clone, model execution, fitting, graph-coordinate coefficient extraction, repository edits, or helpers.

Base for all links: [pinned repository](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/tree/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271). Git tree API returned `truncated:false`. [Input CSV](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/data/fundamentals.csv) matches supplied blob `46d4aa0ba73c4a2942e3f65ac8f663251184616b`, 2113 bytes.

## Exact observations and transformations

| Input/output | Verified definition/timing | Source file |
|---|---|---|
| `linc_vote_imp` | Logit presidential party's imputed national two-party House vote fraction; response is level, not swing or percentage points. | `05_impute_uncontested.R`, CSV |
| `gdp_chg` | FRED GDPC1; quarterly frequency; `pc1` (year-over-year percentage change), latest available quarter in each even year. Historical complete years therefore use Q4; 2022 latest available quarter differs. Not annual-average GDP or annualized quarterly growth. | `01_fred.R` |
| `cpi_chg` | FRED CPIAUCSL, quarterly frequency, `pc1`; latest quarter as above. | `01_fred.R` |
| `lunemp` | FRED UNRATE, quarterly frequency, `log`; natural logarithm of unemployment rate expressed in percentage units (e.g. ln(3.6)), not a fraction or unemployment change. | `01_fred.R`, CSV |
| `lg_approval` | Logit of mean approval fraction in October, or latest available month no later than October, in each even year. Not tenure average, approval trend, net approval, or fixed September observation. | `02_pres_approval.R` |
| `lg_retire` | `qlogis(inc_retire_pct)` from raw national input. CSV alone cannot establish denominator: incumbent-party retirements divided by which eligible incumbents/seats remains unresolved. | `03_fund_basic.R` |
| `inc_house` | 1 if president's party controls House, else0. | `03_fund_basic.R` |
| `dem_pres` | 1 Democratic president, 0 Republican. | README/basic prep |
| `polar` | Previous election's correlation across contested districts of **logit** Democratic House vote and **logit** Democratic presidential vote; drops missing/infinite values; shifts year forward2. | `04_outcomes_house.R` |

[Economy preparation](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/prep-data/01_fred.R), [approval preparation](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/prep-data/02_pres_approval.R), [basic preparation](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/prep-data/03_fund_basic.R), [district preparation](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/prep-data/04_outcomes_house.R).

CSV has 27 even-year rows1970–2022. `linc_vote_imp` is present only1976–2020: 23 fitted national-election observations, split into **11 midterms1978–2018** and12 presidential elections1976–2020. 2022 is prediction input with missing outcome. `nomidterm=0` selects midterms. Model does not fit all1948–2020 midterms:1948–2006 refers to the economy PCA construction cohort, not response-estimation cohort.

## Exact specification; numbers available versus missing

[Build code](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/build/fundamentals.R) uses:

`econ = 0.678*gdp_chg − 0.038*lunemp − 0.734*cpi_chg`

These are **PCA weights**, not fitted election-response coefficients. No standardization is shown; `prcomp` uses its default centering, while subsequent predictor is the literal weighted sum above.

`linc_vote_imp ~ inc_house + polar*(dem_pres + lg_approval) - polar + econ + lg_retire`

Expanded: intercept, House control, Democratic president, logit approval, polarization×Democratic president, polarization×logit approval, economic composite, logit retirement fraction; no standalone polarization term. Separate `brms` Bayesian linear models, no explicit family argument (Gaussian default), R2D2 prior `R2D2(0.6, cons_D2=2)` on coefficient class. Logit-response error spread must remain on that scale; it cannot be copied as vote-share percentage points. Approval response varies with polarization and baseline approval through nonlinear transforms.

The untruncated pinned tree contains **no** `data-raw/produced/fundamentals_model_2022.rds` or `stan/fund_m.rds`, and no exact coefficient/posterior-summary export identified. [.gitignore](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/.gitignore) excludes raw/produced files, general RDS and Stan fitted objects. [README.Rmd](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/README.Rmd) loads the absent fitted object to generate an `mcmc_plot`; [parameter SVG](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/readme-doc/fund_model_est-1.svg) is a plot, not an exact numeric table. No numeric intercept, response coefficients, residual sigma posterior, or their joint draws were extracted or invented.

Tracked `data/fund_pred/fundamentals_pred_{2010,2012,...,2022}.rds` files exist. Build code defines them as `posterior_predict` draws for that year's input after refitting only previous same-type elections. They combine parameter/predictive uncertainty; they are **not pure residual samples**, and cannot predict different fictional covariates without the fitted model. This pass inspected their existence/code provenance, not binary contents.

## Lineage and limitations

Raw approval input is `data-raw/dfp/clean_potus_approval_1941_2022.csv`; national vote/retirement input is `data-raw/dfp/001_house_national_voteshare_input.csv`; controls are `data-raw/manual/party_control.csv`. All absent from pinned tree. `dfp` directory name does not independently identify original pollster, election collector, or exact cleaning vintage. A separate historical-approval acquisition script reads a Google Sheet into `data/past_pres_approval.csv`, but this is not the file used by the inspected fundamentals pipeline; do not claim it completes lineage.

[Imputation code](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/midterms-22/blob/c50e8dd0efd136fd06c92b1e846b8898ced71271/R/prep-data/05_impute_uncontested.R) trains BART on contested **midterm** district elections (stricter than README's general1976–2020 description). National aggregate is weighted by counts of contested/uncontested districts, rather than total ballots, so its outcome is not the raw Clerk national popular vote. An unresolved apparent scale inconsistency is visible: `dem_seat.pred` is already a mean of `plogis` predictions, yet uncontested aggregation calls `mean(plogis(dem_seat.pred))` again. This was not executed, corrected, or used to regenerate data; author clarification is needed before asserting processed-data fidelity.

## Exact missing integration items

1. Source-published fitted intercept, all7 predictor coefficients, Gaussian sigma, and preferably their joint posterior draws/covariance (with model/version/runtime provenance). An SVG-derived approximation or a new reduced regression is not this published model.
2. Defined World producers with compatible units/timing for real GDP YoY quarter, CPI YoY quarter, unemployment level, election-month approval, incumbent-party retirement fraction, House control, party identity, and lagged district-result logit correlation. Repository World coverage was not audited here; these are required contracts, not claims that particular fields are absent.
3. Retirement denominator, raw-source collector/vintage, latest-quarter aggregation convention, and imputation-scale clarification.
4. A separately explicit mapping from predicted national imputed vote **level** to swing/district outcomes and creation-time seeded world calibration. The historical 2022 prediction draws are not reusable runtime response parameters.

The source supplies useful national paired observations and a transparent specification. It does **not** validate independent .45/.6/.35/.2 slopes or an economy-to-approval coefficient2; GDP/unemployment/CPI enter one PCA composite, and approval is an input rather than an economically generated output.

# Complete annual law-output coverage remains missing

No comparable completed-year all-subject dataset covering all 50 states, DC and five territories was located. The accessible Quorum reports remain midyear snapshots. FiscalNote publishes broader tables, but the historical recaps lack a precise cutoff and clear measure exclusions in the readable text. A newer FiscalNote report supplies explicitly completed 2025 regular-session cohorts for four biennial states. These support bounded session examples, not an all-56 annual calibration.

## Directly readable completed-session examples

[FiscalNote 2026 recap](https://fiscalnote.com/reports/2026-states-session-recap-report), published September 1, 2026, data as of August 17, 2026, explicitly marks the following as completed 2025 regular-session figures. Its methodology excludes resolutions, memorials and amendments; counts prefiled bills with their destination session; and defines these cohort rates as enacted bills divided by introduced bills.

| Jurisdiction | Enacted in completed 2025 cohort | Introduced in same cohort |
|---|---:|---:|
| North Dakota | 600 | 1,020 |
| Nevada | 532 | 1,003 |
| Montana | 777 | 1,589 |
| Texas | 1,206 | 7,274 |

The report covers 51 jurisdictions. Its wider tables combine 2026 single-year sessions with 2025 carryover cohorts and completed 2025 biennial sessions; those groups are expressly not directly comparable. The four rows above are its own collector measurement, not independently audited official session totals.

## Historical recaps checked

- [Quorum 2024 PDF](https://www.quorum.us/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/2024-State-Legislative-Trends-Report-Digital-Edition.pdf), January 1–June 30, 2024: 14,088 enacted nationwide; excludes simple/concurrent resolutions. No complete all-jurisdiction enacted table. Page 5 reports Alaska 10, Ohio 13, Missouri 23, North Carolina 29 and Pennsylvania 35, explicitly saying Alaska adjourned in May while Ohio still met year-round. Page 6 gives Arkansas regular-session 181 of 184, separate from a special-session reintroduction. These are cutoff/cohort figures; adjournment does not itself prove completion of subsequent governor actions. No annualization is justified.
- [Quorum 2023 PDF](https://www.quorum.us/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Quorum_2023StateLegislatureReport_Digital-2.pdf), January 1–July 31, 2023: no complete all-jurisdiction enacted table. Page 7 reports Missouri 20 and Alaska 24 and explicitly calls both already adjourned. Page 8 reports Colorado 474 enacted from 623 introduced across its 120-day session. These support named session-scale examples with cutoff caveats, not a nationwide range. The report's nationwide introductions remain internally inconsistent: 104,359 in the intro versus 105,359 in its table.
- [Quorum 2025 PDF](https://www.quorum.us/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2025-State-Legislative-Trends-Report-Digital.pdf), January 1–June 30, 2025: 130,120 introduced excluding carryovers and 15,951 enacted. Simple/concurrent resolutions excluded. Page 5 gives Puerto Rico four enacted bills introduced in 2025; Ohio six new-origin bills but 38 when carryovers are included. Neither is an annual total. Page 6 includes carryovers for its percentage comparison. No full all-56 table or jurisdiction completion flags.
- [FiscalNote 2024 recap](https://fiscalnote.com/reports/2024-state-sessions-recap), published August 21, 2024: claims all 50 states and DC, over 21,000 enactments, and inclusion of special sessions. No precise data-through date, carryover treatment or resolution exclusions established in readable methodology. Embedded all-data visualization: [Datawrapper WRzsL version 2](https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/WRzsL/2/). Its table values did not render through the web reader, and its data.csv endpoint was inaccessible. The report's figures cannot be promoted to exact complete-year bills-only counts.
- [FiscalNote 2025 recap](https://fiscalnote.com/reports/2025-state-sessions-recap), published July 29, 2025: nearly 29,000 enactments, but explicitly lists eight states still in session. No completed-year all-56 measure. Special sessions included; precise carryover and resolution treatment unestablished here.

## Remaining coverage

American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands and U.S. Virgin Islands annual all-subject enactment totals remain missing from every located nationwide report. DC appears in FiscalNote coverage but its completed annual cohort is not established. Puerto Rico appears in Quorum examples, but full annual coverage is unestablished. Do not fill absent counts with zero, apply a common territory value, extrapolate partial-year counts, or combine different collectors' definitions into a comparable series.

Source research only on September 29, 2026. No repository, claims, Git or runtime jobs changed. This is an internal evidence handoff; no owner-report reviewer was run under the no-helper constraint.

# Vermont completed 2025 regular-session Act cohort — bounded source handoff

Research date: 2026-09-29. Internal source handoff only; parent owns integration. No repository edits or helpers. Six unique primary-source targets inspected/attempted (including two unsuccessful opens); no national collector search.

## Established measure

**73 numbered Acts in Vermont's official 2025 Act Summary Book**, prepared by the Office of Legislative Counsel. Extraction found 73 distinct `Act No.` headings, exactly integers 1–73 with no gaps. This is a document-cohort count, not a count of bills introduced, resolutions, provisions, or a claimed all-session calendar-year total.

Source: [2025 Act Summary Book v2](https://legislature.vermont.gov/assets/Legislative-Reports/2025_Act_Summary_book-v2.pdf), 52 PDF pages. Cover identifies the 2025 Vermont General Assembly and Office of Legislative Counsel. First heading Act 1 (H.78), last heading Act 73 (H.454), PDF page 49. Extraction read the whole document using overlapping text windows, deduplicated Act headings, and checked the full 1–73 sequence. The book's disclaimer says summaries may not be exhaustive; therefore this handoff treats the count as the book's numbered-Act cohort rather than independently certified statutory completeness.

## Official cutoff and post-adjournment enactment

[June 16, 2025 Senate Journal](https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2026/Docs/JOURNAL/sj250616.pdf), PDF pages 113–116 (printed journal pages 2005–2008), supplies final-adjournment and post-adjournment messages:

- J.R.S.28 directs June 16/17 adjournment until a joint recall, if needed, or January 6, 2026. Senate actually adjourned June 16 at 7:40 p.m.; this is adjournment of the first half of the biennium, not termination of the 2025–2026 biennial legislature.
- The House completion message explicitly identifies the first half of the Biennial Session.
- Post-adjournment appended messages record governor approval of H.474 on June 25, H.480 on June 27, and H.454 on July 1, 2025. Thus June 16 legislative adjournment cannot be used as the enactment-date cutoff for this cohort.

[Official H.454 / Act 73 status](https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/H.454) labels the cohort Regular Session 2025–2026 and reports governor approval July 1, 2025. Its UI attaches that later approval message to the June 16 legislative date; use the actual approval date stated in the message. The Senate Journal independently confirms July 1.

[Official J.R.S.28 status](https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/J.R.S.28) identifies Act R-188 and adoption June 16, 2025 (search-readable; direct open failed). Resolution numbering is separate from numbered laws and R-188 is excluded from the 73-Act count.

## Limits / safe integration label

Use **“2025 regular-session numbered Acts in official summary book: 73; legislative adjournment June 16, with governor approvals through at least July 1.”** This provides completed regular-session output evidence without annualizing it.

- The inspected sources do not expressly certify absence of a later 2025 recall or special-session enactment. Do not promote 73 to an independently verified all-session calendar-year total.
- The book has no explicit publication/as-of date on its cover; vintage is title-year 2025, file variant v2, accessed September 29, 2026.
- No introduced-bill denominator or passage percentage was established. Resolution counts were not inventoried.
- No claim that pending bills could not carry into 2026: the journal expressly describes the first half of the biennium and provides for reconvening.

## 2024 cross-check, not a count

[2024 Act Summary Book](https://legislature.vermont.gov/assets/Legislative-Reports/2024_Act_Summary_book.pdf) begins Act 82 (S.160), reflecting numbering continued from 2023. A final Act number therefore cannot be read as a 2024 annual total. This bounded pass did not finish a full 2024 heading inventory.

An additional official [2024 governor action-list target](https://governor.vermont.gov/governor-scotts-blog/action-taken-governor-scott-bills-during-2024-legislative-session) failed direct retrieval and supplies no count used here.

descriptiveAnchors.denominator: CPS self-reported citizen voting-age population, not registered voters or administrative ballots. Survey estimates are subject to sampling and reporting error.

limits: These are descriptive election-type, registration and geography observations, not causal responses to presidential approval, candidate quality, economy or mobilization.
The state table covers 50 states and DC, not territories or county/town-size bins. It does not establish a broad settlement-size adjustment.
No game coefficient, hard outcome bound, response distribution or new saved-world sampling law is approved by these observations.
Do not assign turnout from one place or treat absent registration/education evidence as zero. Missing causal and size evidence stays open.
Existing unsupported mood weights remain WIP; no production source, schema or election behavior changed.
currentResearchScope.nextEvidence: Broad causal driver and settlement-size evidence remains pending. Team9 bill-number quick research has priority; no duplicate helper or fitted-model request is opened.
